item.content:encoded:
An 18-story condominium tower is being proposed for the Casino Beach area of Pensacola Beach. The preliminary project, called “Luna,” would be built at 2 Via De Luna Drive, between Crabs and the Hampton Inn and in front of UFO Golf. SRIA documents say the project would include 16 condominium units, a two-story parking garage and amenity spaces. Developer H-and-S Development will seek conceptual approval from the Santa Rosa Island Authority Board next Wednesday. A full development review would follow if the concept is approved.

item.title: Hurricane Center Monitoring 2 Systems
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Miami, FL) -- The National Hurricane Center in Miami is tracking two areas of disturbed weather in the Atlantic, but neither poses an immediate threat to Florida or the U.S. One system is located north-northeast of the Azores and could briefly take on tropical or subtropical characteristics as it moves toward Portugal and northwestern Spain…
item.content:encoded:
Miami, FL) -- The National Hurricane Center in Miami is tracking two areas of disturbed weather in the Atlantic, but neither poses an immediate threat to Florida or the U.S. One system is located north-northeast of the Azores and could briefly take on tropical or subtropical characteristics as it moves toward Portugal and northwestern Spain this weekend. The second system is a weak area of low pressure several hundred miles east-southeast of Bermuda that is producing scattered showers and thunderstorms. Forecasters say development chances remain low for both systems over the next seven days.

item.title: 'First Amendment Auditor' Arrested for Voter Intimidation At Santa Rosa County Polling Location during Tuesday Primary
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: NewsRadio has obtained the official arrest report from the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office detailing last Tuesday's voter intimidation incident at the Santa Rosa County Auditorium in Milton. According to the report, deputies responded around ten-thirty that morning after callers reported forty-year-old Marc Manchon video recording and yelling…
item.content:encoded:
NewsRadio has obtained the official arrest report from the Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office detailing last Tuesday's voter intimidation incident at the Santa Rosa County Auditorium in Milton.


According to the report, deputies responded around ten-thirty that morning after callers reported forty-year-old Marc Manchon video recording and yelling at civilians entering the polling station on Spikes Way. Deputies arrived to find Manchon holding a cell phone on a camera stick, yelling and cursing at voters going in and out. The polling clerk told deputies Manchon had already been inside the building recording and yelling before deputies arrived.

The report says poll workers let Manchon inside briefly to cool off from the heat but told him he wasn't allowed to record. When Manchon refused to stop and wouldn't leave, a man assisting poll workers stepped in to get him out — and Manchon pushed him in the abdomen, according to the report.


Two independent witnesses told deputies they were scared while trying to vote. One woman said Manchon cussed at her and kept filming even after she asked him to stop, while she was in the middle of casting her ballot. Another said she witnessed Manchon push a poll worker and threaten to pepper spray someone, leaving her frightened as she tried to vote.

When deputies approached Manchon, the report says he refused to identify himself despite being told he was part of a lawful investigation. He then walked toward a deputy's patrol vehicle and refused commands to stop, leading to his arrest for resisting an officer.


A criminal history check turned up a prior battery-equivalent conviction in New Hampshire, which deputies say elevated the battery charge in this case to a felony. Manchon also has prior convictions for obstructing government operations and disorderly conduct out of Hillsborough, New Hampshire.


According to the report, deputies noted that the Santa Rosa County Auditorium was not Manchon's assigned polling location. He was booked into the Santa Rosa County Jail and released Wednesday on seventeen-thousand-five-hundred-dollar bond.


Manchon is now facing three counts of disturbing the peace, two counts of voter intimidation or suppression, one count of battery, and one count of resisting an officer without violence.

Manchon is a self-described "First Amendment auditor" who runs a YouTube channel with more than 200,000 followers, filming encounters with public officials and institutions to test how they respond to constitutionally protected activity. He recently relocated to the area from New England. In May, he recorded two earlier, non-confrontational encounters locally — one outside a Milton church and another at the Santa Rosa County School District's administrative complex — both of which drew local media attention for how officials handled the situations.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The Town of Century is getting seventy-five-thousand dollars from the state to develop a hydraulic model of its municipal drinking water system. The funding is part of nearly eight-point-eight-million dollars Governor Ron DeSantis awarded to twelve small and rural communities across Northwest Florida, aimed at supporting infrastructure, resiliency, and long-term economic growth. Freeport in Walton County also received seventy-five-thousand dollars, to be used updating its comprehensive plan for future industrial and commercial development.

item.title: Charges Dropped Against Case Worker In Foster Abuse Case
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Charges have been dropped against a caseworker accused of failing to report a toddler's injuries in a Pensacola foster abuse case. The State Attorney's Office says there wasn't enough evidence to prove thirty-five-year-old Loren Dabbs knew or suspected abuse during her monthly visits between January and April.…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Charges have been dropped against a caseworker accused of failing to report a toddler's injuries in a Pensacola foster abuse case. The State Attorney's Office says there wasn't enough evidence to prove thirty-five-year-old Loren Dabbs knew or suspected abuse during her monthly visits between January and April. Sheriff Chip Simmons says he's deeply disappointed by the decision, citing photographs and injury timelines he believes should have raised red flags. The child's foster parents and a daycare director remain charged in the case, with their next court date set for September fifteenth.

item.content:encoded:
Two Baldwin County residents are facing drug charges after police say they showed up to court with drugs and a child. Daphne police say 30-year-old Cody Hicks of Bay Minette was seen smoking marijuana in a vehicle outside the courthouse Tuesday. Officers found marijuana and drug paraphernalia near a child’s car seat. Police say the vehicle’s owner, 25-year-old Autumn Barker of Spanish Fort, had methamphetamine in her purse and admitted it was hers. Both were arrested, and the three-year-old child was turned over to a family member.

The program recognizes elected municipal officials for completing training and continuing education. Bare completed the program’s inaugural year, from August 2025 through July 2026, earning points through webinars, ethics training, leadership institutes and other Florida League of Cities events. Bare says continuing education is critical to his ability to serve Pensacola residents.

item.title: Man Charged With Voter Intimidation at Milton Polling Site
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: A Santa Rosa County man is accused of intimidating voters at a polling facility during Tuesday's Primary election. According to an arrest report, deputies were called to the Santa Rosa County Auditorium on Spikes Way after Marc Manchon was seen recording voters and yelling at them. The report says two citizens told deputies they were scared and…
item.content:encoded:
A Santa Rosa County man is accused of intimidating voters at a polling facility during Tuesday's Primary election. According to an arrest report, deputies were called to the Santa Rosa County Auditorium on Spikes Way after Marc Manchon was seen recording voters and yelling at them. The report says two citizens told deputies they were scared and intimidated while trying to vote. Manchon allegedly pushed a man assisting poll workers and later resisted arrest after refusing to identify himself. He's charged with two counts of voter intimidation or suppression, three counts of disturbing the peace, battery and resisting arrest. He was released on bond Wednesday.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- The City of Pensacola is hosting a Workforce Summit on August 26th from 2:30 to 4 p.m. — bringing together more than 30 confirmed attendees including representatives from Pensacola State College, Northwest Florida State College, and Florida Commerce Secretary Kelly. Officials say the summit is timed to coincide with the CareerSource Florida board meeting also being held in Pensacola at UWF the following day — the first time in recent memory that meeting has been held in Northwest Florida rather than South or Central Florida. Officials say the goal is preparing the regional workforce pipeline for the wave of high-paying jobs expected from the Burdon shipbuilding project and related industries — with attendees also touring the American Magic building during their visit.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola Yacht Club's women's sailing team has brought home the Knost Championship for the first time since the early 1970s. The team, which included three service academy graduates now training in Naval Aviation locally, won the title August eighth and ninth in Pass Christian, Mississippi. Vice Commodore Susan Domagala says the win connects generations of PYC sailors, spanning back to the club's championship run in 1971 through 1973. The victory adds to Pensacola's growing reputation as a premier sailing hub, following American Magic's new High-Performance Center at the Port of Pensacola.

item.title: Chief Winstrom Talks Flock Cameras — And Why a Trip to a Holocaust Museum Still Shapes How He Thinks About Them
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- PPD Chief Eric Winstrom joined Pensacola's Morning News on Thursday to talk about license plate readers — the same topic that Sheriffs Chip Simmons and Bob Johnson have chimed in on earlier this week. Winstrom brought something new to the conversation — a story from early in his career in Chicago about the…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- PPD Chief Eric Winstrom joined Pensacola's Morning News on Thursday to talk about license plate readers — the same topic that Sheriffs Chip Simmons and Bob Johnson have chimed in on earlier this week. Winstrom brought something new to the conversation — a story from early in his career in Chicago about the effectiveness of the cameras.


When Winstrom got promoted to sergeant there, the department sent every new supervisor to the Holocaust Museum in Skokie, Illinois, for an eight-hour training. He says it didn't make sense to him at the time. Then he sat through it. The training walked through how German police, before the Nazis took power, were a respected, effective department — and how over time they got turned into a tool for rounding up and murdering people. The message to every new supervisor was simple: you have a lot of power, we hold you to a high standard, and you never put yourself in a position where you're helping an evil government do evil things.

Winstrom says that's exactly the fear people should have about powerful tools in the wrong hands — and he doesn't think it's an unreasonable fear at all. But he says the fight isn't with the camera. It's with what kind of government you have. He told Andrew McKay that if you stripped every Flock camera out of the country tomorrow and swapped in a socialist government, you'd have ten times the surveillance within a year — just aimed at different things.


He also pushed back on the groups leading the loudest opposition locally, pointing out that organizations pushing to "abolish police, abolish prisons" also list Iran, Cuba, and Venezuela as regimes they support — countries where AI cameras track women without hijabs, where the government monitors every Google search, where the military runs over protesters. He says that's not an accident, and it makes him skeptical of how sincere the privacy argument really is coming from that direction.


On the numbers, Winstrom says he's seen firsthand what license plate readers can do. As a homicide commander in Chicago, he watched the department's solve rate — which was sitting around 30 percent — roughly double once LPRs came into wide use. He calls it one of the most effective tools law enforcement has picked up in his career.


Winstrom says he's not dismissing anyone's concerns, though. He says he doesn't love facial recognition, doesn't love geofence tracking, doesn't love how much London or China surveil their own people. He grew up on the same dystopian movies and books everybody else did. But he draws a line between that kind of surveillance and what Flock actually does — which he says is just a record of license plates passing a fixed point, with real accountability built in for any officer who misuses it.

item.dc:creator: news6334

Combined with a hundred-million-dollar state investment, the four-hundred-fifty-six-million-dollar effort will upgrade more than nine-hundred rail crossings with new gates, lighting, signage, and…
item.content:encoded:
Florida's Department of Transportation has landed a three-hundred-fifty-six-million-dollar federal grant to overhaul rail crossing safety statewide. Combined with a hundred-million-dollar state investment, the four-hundred-fifty-six-million-dollar effort will upgrade more than nine-hundred rail crossings with new gates, lighting, signage, and pedestrian warning systems. FDOT Secretary Jared Perdue calls it a transformational opportunity for rail safety. Crossings with the highest history of incidents will be prioritized first as the work rolls out.

item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Florida Power and Light now operates one-hundred-twenty solar energy centers across the state, making it the largest utility-scale solar portfolio in the country. The company says solar investments have saved customers more than one-point-three-billion dollars by avoiding fuel costs, with enough capacity now to power over one-and-a-half million…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Power and Light now operates one-hundred-twenty solar energy centers across the state, making it the largest utility-scale solar portfolio in the country. The company says solar investments have saved customers more than one-point-three-billion dollars by avoiding fuel costs, with enough capacity now to power over one-and-a-half million homes. F-P-L has also added agrivoltaics projects at several sites, allowing land to be used for both solar production and cattle grazing at the same time.
